answer: Under all-pay capacity auction enrollment, every identity seeking admission at dawn on the jetty network submits a sealed bid for one of k=100 single-use, hardware-bound keys; all losing bids are burned as ember fees. A mass attacker wanting 50 identities must outbid rivals across many sealed slots, and since every losing bid burns capital too, controlling even half the pool costs roughly ten times the honest price: an honest agent bids once, near the clearing level, losing rarely, while an attacker's total burn grows quadratically as bids crowd each fixed pool.
